key_insight: Neural-network models applied to text embeddings can quantify levels of peace from online news (and, partially, social media), and these models generalize across different news datasets; the authors also built online tools to help users understand and improve their media diets to promote peace.
problem_solved: Lack of scalable, quantitative tools to measure national/local levels of peace from noisy online sources and to provide actionable, user-facing interventions that promote peaceful media consumption.
method: Extract text embeddings from online news sources and feed them to neural-network models to predict a "peace" score.
Train on one news-media dataset and evaluate cross-dataset generalization to demonstrate transferability and robustness.

Develop online user tools that analyze individual media diets and provide feedback designed to foster more peaceful information consumption (social-media application to platforms like YouTube is indicated in the paper; abstract provided was truncated).
impact: Provides a replicable, scalable approach for ML practitioners and policy analysts to monitor peace using text-based signals and to build user-centered interventions; demonstrates model transferability across datasets, a key practical concern for deployment.
visual_elements: World map heatmap showing predicted peace scores by country
Pipeline diagram: news/social media → text embeddings → neural network → peace score dashboard
Bar/line chart comparing model performance on source vs. target news datasets (illustrating generalization)
Mockup of the online "media-diet" tool/dashboard that gives users personalized feedback and suggested actions
paper_title: Measuring and Fostering Peace through Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence
paper_authors: P. Gilda, P. Dungarwal, A. Thongkham, E. T. Ajayi, S. Choudhary
